<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
VS Code's notebook browser exposes internal `hiddenFoldingRanges` and `setHiddenAreas` APIs. These could be used to hide cells.

Direct access to VS Code's internal folding APIs likely requires a proposed API, so that path seems blocked. A custom notebook editor would be overkill. The pragmatic plan is to physically delete the tagged cells from the document when hiding is active, storing a serialized backup in the extension context keyed by notebook URI and cell index. Restoring cells happens when showing them again.

The physical deletion approach carries significant risks. Cell indices shift during edits, and saving without careful restoration could permanently lose hidden cells. The focus is shifting to public VS Code APIs instead. The plan is to search for notebook decoration or hidden area APIs, check the engine version in package.json, and look at how other open-source extensions handle cell hiding.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The stable VS Code API does not appear to include `inputCollapsed`. It may only exist in the proposed API or through cell metadata.

CSS injection via extensions is not natively supported by VS Code. A temporary cell deletion approach with memento backup is being considered instead.

Cell data would be serialized and stored in workspace state before deletion. Hidden cells could be restored at their original indices when toggled back visible. To prevent accidental data loss, the extension could subscribe to `onWillSaveNotebookDocument` to temporarily reveal all hidden cells during a save operation.

Several edge cases still need handling: switching between notebooks, adding or removing `remove-cell` tags while cells are hidden, and multiple open notebooks. Using internal APIs for editor decorations was considered but rejected for marketplace distribution. The next step is to search existing VS Code issues for notebook cell hiding functionality.

VS Code's interactive window already provides `interactiveWindow.collapseCellInputCode`, which offers a useful reference pattern. The desired user experience is a preview-mode authoring workflow where `remove-cell` cells stay in the file but are hidden until a toolbar toggle reveals them. This confirms the delete-and-restore approach risks losing data on save unless cells are temporarily reinserted during the save event.

Re-hiding cells after a successful save is another option if the toggle is off. A custom serializer or content provider is too heavy. Replacing cell content with empty text and zero-height decorations would still leave cell chrome visible. The README phrase "factor-out cells" likely means literally moving cells to another file rather than hiding them.

Checking whether Microsoft Jupyter has built-in support for this feature. A notebook renderer could potentially inspect cell metadata tags. Another approach under consideration is using zero-height text decorations with collapsed outputs, though this would still leave a status bar bar visible.

A thin expandable placeholder row was considered as a compromise, but the user expects cells to fully disappear when hidden and reappear when toggled back on. The idea of using VS Code's Folding feature to collapse cells into hidden ranges was also explored, though persisting those ranges across sessions remains uncertain.

VS Code issue 125308 is being reviewed for context on notebook cell expansion and collapse. The implementation plan centers on a `RemoveCellHidingManager` that uses soft-delete with a save round-trip. A `RemoveCellSnapshot` would store each cell's index, kind, source, language, metadata, and outputs. Hidden cells would be tracked per-notebook in global or workspace state. On notebook open or change, cells tagged with `remove-cell` would be identified via `getCellTags()`.

Deletion will proceed from highest to lowest indices to preserve original positions. Snapshots will be stored for later re-insertion. The toggle command will be `jupyter-cell-tags.removeCell.toggleHiddenCellsVisibility`, defaulting to hide mode. A context key `jupyter-cell-tags.removeCell.hiddenMode` will drive the toolbar button state.

The toggle will use `enablement` and switch between `$(eye)` and `$(eye-closed)` icons. Event listeners for `onDidChangeNotebookDocument`, `onDidChangeActiveNotebookEditor`, and `onDidOpenNotebookDocument` will sync hidden states. The toolbar action will be registered under `notebook/toolbar` in `package.json`. Hidden cells naturally skip execution in "Run All" because they are removed from the document model. Restored cells will retain their execution outputs from snapshots. Workspace state keys by notebook URI, so untitled notebooks are supported.

Deleting cells breaks undo history. Reverting a deletion would corrupt the hidden state. Keeping cells in the document and hiding them with CSS was considered, but VS Code offers no standard API for notebook-level CSS injection. The possibility of injecting CSS via extension code is now being explored.

Webview panels and color customizations were ruled out as unsuitable for notebook cells. A custom notebook editor was considered too heavy. The remaining options are temporary cell deletion with save guards, or collapsing cells with a placeholder status bar.

Partial hiding is being kept as a fallback if full deletion proves too risky. The proposed API `NotebookEditor.setDecorations` with a full-cell overlay is being evaluated for VS Code 1.98. The extension manifest and TypeScript configuration are being checked for enabled API proposals.

Collapsing cells leaves visible cell chrome, so that approach is insufficient. Visual-only text decorations would also fail to hide markdown previews and outputs. Delete-and-restore remains the only viable method.

A new module `src/removeCell/removeCellHiding.ts` will manage the feature. It defines a constant for the `remove-cell` tag. State will track whether the toggle is enabled and store snapshots per notebook URI. The toggle will switch between hiding and showing tagged cells.

The implementation will delete cells from highest to lowest index to preserve snapshot positions, then restore them from lowest to highest. A toggle command handler will orchestrate the hide and show cycles.

The interaction flow is now clear. Adding the tag to a visible cell deletes it on the next refresh. Removing the tag requires toggling show first. Showing restores all snapshots and allows editing tags. Hiding again re-scans and deletes tagged cells. An `isApplyingHide` flag will prevent the system from reacting to its own deletions during save operations.

The save logic will use `onWillSaveNotebookDocument` to restore hidden cells before saving, then `onDidSaveNotebookDocument` to re-hide them afterward. Whether `onDidSaveNotebookDocument` exists in the API still needs verification.

This feature will use **temporary removal from the open document** plus **save-roundtrip restoration** so tagged cells remain in the saved `.ipynb`.\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TD\n  OpenNb[Notebook opened] --\u003e Scan[Scan cells for remove-cell tag]\n  Scan --\u003e|hide mode ON| Snapshot[Snapshot cell data + original index]\n  Snapshot --\u003e Delete[NotebookEdit.deleteCells]\n  ToggleShow[Toolbar toggle: Show] --\u003e Restore[NotebookEdit.insertCells from snapshots]\n  ToggleHide[Toolbar toggle: Hide] --\u003e Snapshot\n  Save[onWillSaveNotebookDocument] --\u003e RestoreSave[Restore hidden cells before write]\n  RestoreSave --\u003e WriteDisk[Save full notebook to disk]\n  WriteDisk --\u003e Rehide[onDidSaveNotebookDocument: re-apply hiding if mode ON]\n```\n\n## Approach\n\n### 1. New module: `src/removeCell/`\n\n| File | Responsibility |\n|---|---|\n| [`src/removeCell/constants.ts`](src/removeCell/constants.ts) | `REMOVE_CELL_TAG = 'remove-cell'` |\n| [`src/removeCell/cellSnapshot.ts`](src/removeCell/cellSnapshot.ts) | `toCellData(cell)` / `toSnapshot(cell)` using `NotebookCellData` (kind, value, languageId, metadata, outputs, executionSummary) |\n| [`src/removeCell/RemoveCellHidingManager.ts`](src/removeCell/RemoveCellHidingManager.ts) | Core state + apply/restore logic |\n| [`src/removeCell/startup.ts`](src/removeCell/startup.ts) | Register command, listeners, context keys |\n\n**Tag detection** — reuse [`getCellTags()`](src/helper.ts):\n\n```typescript\ngetCellTags(cell).includes(REMOVE_CELL_TAG)\n```\n\n**Per-notebook state** (keyed by `notebook.uri.toString()`):\n\n- `snapshots: { originalIndex: number; data: NotebookCellData }[]`\n- `applied: boolean` — cells currently removed from the open document\n- `isApplying: boolean` — guard to ignore our own `onDidChangeNotebookDocument` events\n\n**Apply hiding** (`applyHiding(notebook)`):\n\n1. If already applied or no tagged cells, return.\n2. Collect tagged cells with current indices; sort **descending** by index.\n3. Snapshot each cell, then `NotebookEdit.deleteCells` in one `WorkspaceEdit`.\n4. Set `applied = true`, update context key.\n\n**Restore** (`restoreHiddenCells(notebook)`):\n\n1. Insert snapshots **ascending** by `originalIndex` via `NotebookEdit.insertCells`.\n2. Clear `applied`, clear snapshots for that notebook.\n\n**Toggle command** `jupyter-cell-tags.removeCell.toggleVisibility`:\n\n- Global hide mode stored in `ExtensionContext.globalState` (`removeCell.hideEnabled`, default **`true`** per your preference).\n- When turning **on**: `applyHiding` on active notebook (and any tracked open notebooks).\n- When turning **off**: `restoreHiddenCells`.\n- Update toolbar context: `jupyter-cell-tags.removeCell.hideEnabled`.\n\n**Save safety** (critical):\n\n```typescript\nworkspace.onWillSaveNotebookDocument(e =\u003e {\n  if (manager.isApplied(e.notebook)) {\n    e.waitUntil(manager.restoreHiddenCells(e.notebook));\n  }\n});\nworkspace.onDidSaveNotebookDocument(notebook =\u003e {\n  if (manager.shouldRehide(notebook)) {\n    manager.applyHiding(notebook);\n  }\n});\n```\n\n**Lifecycle listeners** (debounced ~150ms, matching other modules):\n\n- `onDidOpenNotebookDocument` — apply hiding if mode ON\n- `onDidChangeActiveNotebookEditor` — sync toolbar context (e.g. count of hidden cells)\n- `onDidChangeNotebookDocument` — when mode ON and not `isApplying`: if a visible cell gains `remove-cell`, hide it; reconcile after external undo\n\n**Deactivate** — restore all notebooks with applied hiding before disposal.\n\n### 2. Wire activation\n\nIn [`src/extension.ts`](src/extension.ts): import and call `activateRemoveCellHiding(context)` alongside existing modules.\n\n### 3. `package.json` contributions\n\n**Command**\n\n- `jupyter-cell-tags.removeCell.toggleVisibility`\n- Title: `Toggle Remove-Cell Visibility`\n- Icon: `$(eye-closed)` when hidden (click to show), `$(eye)` when shown — implement via **two menu entries** with complementary `when` clauses on context `jupyter-cell-tags.removeCell.hideEnabled`, or update icon/title in the command handler via `vscode.commands.executeCommand` pattern used elsewhere.\n\n**Toolbar** — add to [`package.json`](package.json) `notebook/toolbar` (group `navigation/execute@9`):\n\n```json\n{\n  \"command\": \"jupyter-cell-tags.removeCell.toggleVisibility\",\n  \"group\": \"navigation/execute@9\",\n  \"when\": \"notebookType == jupyter-notebook\"\n}\n```\n\n**Setting** (optional, small scope):\n\n- `jupyter-cell-tags.removeCell.enabled` (default `true`) — master switch to disable the feature\n\n**Activation events**: `onCommand:jupyter-cell-tags.removeCell.toggleVisibility`\n\n**Context keys** set at runtime:\n\n- `jupyter-cell-tags.removeCell.hideEnabled` — drives toggle icon/state\n- `jupyter-cell-tags.removeCell.hasHiddenCells` — optional `when` to dim button when notebook has no tagged cells\n\n### 4. Edge cases\n\n| Case | Handling |\n|---|---|\n| Save while hidden | Restore before save, re-hide after (cells persist on disk) |\n| Close without save | VS Code reverts to disk copy; snapshots discarded |\n| Undo after hide | Reconcile on `onDidChangeNotebookDocument` |\n| Tagged cell added while hidden | Debounced re-scan → snapshot + delete |\n| Run All / run groups | Hidden cells absent from model → naturally skipped (nbconvert parity) |\n| Git diff / outline / tree views | Indices shift while hidden — acceptable; document limitation |\n| Non-`jupyter-notebook` types | Only register for `jupyter-notebook` |\n\n### 5. Short answer: **not in a practical way for normal `.ipynb` editing in VS Code.**

There are two different “notebook provider/renderer” concepts in VS Code, and neither lets you override the Jupyter notebook UI to hide cells by tag.

## 1. Notebook **Renderer** (not what you want)

`contributes.notebookRenderer` only renders **cell outputs** (HTML, images, custom MIME types). It does **not** control:

- which cells appear in the notebook
- the cell list / editor chrome
- markdown/code cell editing

So a custom renderer cannot implement `remove-cell` hiding.

## 2. Notebook **Serializer / Provider** (closer, but still not a drop-in override)

`vscode.workspace.registerNotebookSerializer()` defines a **new notebook type** (e.g. `my-notebook`), with:

- `deserializeNotebook()` — bytes → `NotebookData`
- `serializeNotebook()` — `NotebookData` → bytes

You *could* filter cells in `deserializeNotebook()`:

```typescript
// hypothetical — only if YOU own this notebook type
cells.filter(c => !c.metadata?.tags?.includes('remove-cell'))
```

But you **cannot replace** the built-in `jupyter-notebook` provider that `ms-toolsai.jupyter` owns for `.ipynb` files. Extensions don’t get to “rewrite” another extension’s serializer.

Your repo doesn’t register any serializer today — `onNotebook:pho-notebook` in `package.json` is only an activation event, with no `notebooks` contribution or `registerNotebookSerializer` in `src/`.

## What a custom serializer would actually require

| Requirement | Problem |
|---|---|
| Own the notebook type | You’d need a separate type (e.g. `pho-notebook`), not `jupyter-notebook` |
| Open `.ipynb` with your type | Conflicts with Jupyter’s file association unless users change editor associations |
| Kernel / execution | Jupyter extension is wired to `jupyter-notebook`; your type may not get kernels, run buttons, variables view, etc. |
| Save round-trip | Filtered-out cells must be stored somewhere or they’re lost on save |
| Toggle show/hide | Serializer runs on open/save, not continuously — you’d still need runtime state + re-open or document edits |

So a custom provider is a **parallel notebook system**, not a layer on top of the default Jupyter editor.

## 3. Custom Notebook **Editor** (full reimplementation)

`contributes.customEditors` or a fully custom webview notebook would let you render whatever you want, but you’d be rebuilding editing, execution, outputs, undo, diffing, etc. That’s far beyond this extension’s scope.

## 4. What VS Code actually exposes to extensions

For the standard `jupyter-notebook` editor, extensions can:

- read/write cells via `WorkspaceEdit` + `NotebookEdit`
- add toolbar items, status bars, tree views
- decorate cell text editors (not hide whole cells)
- listen to document/selection events

There is **no public API** to say “hide cell index 3 in the notebook list without deleting it.” That’s why the plan used temporary delete + save-time restore.

## Bottom line

- **Custom notebook renderer:** no — wrong abstraction (outputs only).
- **Custom notebook serializer that overrides Jupyter:** no — you can’t replace `ms-toolsai.jupyter`’s provider for normal `.ipynb` use.
- **Custom serializer as a separate notebook type:** possible in theory, but high cost, poor Jupyter integration, and still awkward for live show/hide toggling.

For `remove-cell` in the normal Jupyter notebook experience, **document-level temporary removal with save restoration** (or a future VS Code “cell visibility” API if one appears) is the realistic path.

If you want, I can outline what a `pho-notebook` serializer prototype would look like and exactly where it would break down with the Jupyter extension — still in Ask mode, or switch to Agent mode to implement the planned approach.
